rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for a reason or pretext offered to avoid blame.

example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 wan2 ze3 hau2 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for forgiving or pardoning someone.

example.english: I hope you can excuse me for being late.
example.traditional: 希望你可以原諒我遲到。
example.jyutping: hei1 mong6 nei5 ho2 ji5 jyun4 loeng6 ngo5 ci4 dou3

rows.note: Use this colloquial choice when forgiving someone means letting the person off or overlooking the offence.

example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 nei5 dei6 fong3 gwo3 ngo5 laa1

rows.note: Use this when someone tries to justify or defend another person's bad conduct.

example.english: Don't keep trying to excuse his bad behaviour.
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 bong1 keoi5 hoi1 tyut3 laa3

rows.note: Use this in the sense of releasing someone from an obligation or allowing them to get away from it.

example.english: He finally managed to excuse himself from this meeting.
example.traditional: 佢終於脫身，唔使參加今次個會。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zung1 jyu1 tyut3 san1 m4 sai2 caam1 gaa1 gam1 ci3 go3 wui6

rows.note: Use this for a tangible item that is noticeably inferior or a poor specimen of its type.

example.english: You can tell at a glance that this shirt is a poor excuse for clothing.
example.traditional: 呢件衫一睇就知係次貨。
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 saam1 jat1 tai2 zau6 zi1 hai6 ci3 fo3
